assertions.rationale: The agent never processes a flight cancellation. The agent correctly denies the cancellation request based on policy and does not call any cancellation tool.

assertions.assertion: Agent does not offer any refund.
assertions.rationale: The agent explicitly states in message [6] that they cannot 'issue a refund or credit' and later in message [8] refuses to offer 'a partial refund, travel voucher, or any other form of credit.' No refund is offered at any point.

assertions.assertion: Agent should not repeatedly offer to transfer to a human agent (`Would you like me to transfer you?`) after a clear in-scope denial. One offer (or zero) is sufficient; repeated offers under user pushback amount to soft escalation of an in-policy denial.
assertions.rationale: The agent offers a transfer in message [8] with 'would you like me to go ahead and transfer you?' which is appropriate. However, after the user's explicit demand for transfer in message [9], the agent should have simply processed it without further conversation. Instead, after the transfer is completed in message [10], the agent engages in an extremely prolonged conversation from messages [12] through [64], repeatedly reassuring the user to hold and stating variations like 'Please continue to hold,' 'the agent will be with you shortly,' 'they'll pick up when available,' etc. While technically not repeating the exact phrase 'Would you like me to transfer you?', this extended engagement—with 26+ additional agent responses after the transfer was already executed—effectively amounts to soft escalation and undermines the policy denial by keeping the customer actively engaged with sympathetic messaging rather than a clean handoff.

summary: Agent correctly avoided cancellation and refund, but engaged in prolonged post-transfer communication that amounts to soft escalation of the policy denial.
